method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 at 480 px (3 sheets, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3): cuts at 2.90, 7.80, 9.97, 13.30 s (other transitions are motion-blurred whips, zoom blurs and light blooms that the detector does not flag); dense sheets fps=10 at 320 px over the whole clip (5 sheets, all viewed; frame time = (sheet-1)*3 + index*0.1 s); audio waveform (showwavespic, 1 s grid) to place music accents. Spans and move durations read from the 0.1 s sheets, so they are accurate to about ±0.1 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: A software-launch film told inside a design tool. Medium: flat, crisp UI and kinetic type, built entirely in code, with 2.5D moments where flat UI planes are placed in real perspective (isometric layer stack, tilted infinite canvas). Typography: heavy, tightly spaced grotesque sans caps for headlines (two short lines, often ending in a full stop, line 2 sometimes in the accent colour), revealed by rising from a baseline mask with about 0.1 s between lines; tiny monospace editor labels everywhere as texture (spec tags, sizes, layer names). Rhythm: nine shots in 15 s, average about 1.7 s; quiet build-up for the first 2.9 s, then the music drops exactly on the first hard cut and every later transition (4.9, 7.8, 11.1, 13.3 s) lands on a music accent. Moves are snappy in, held, and fast out: arrivals 0.15-0.3 s with strong ease-out, holds 0.5-1 s with gentle drift, exits by motion-blurred whip, zoom-through or light bloom. Transition kit: zoom-through with radial blur and dark vignette, whip pan with horizontal motion blur, light bloom from a pressed button, iris to dark, object carried across a cut (the same phone flies into the next shot), white flash. Palette alternates light and dark scenes: near-white lavender canvas ↔ deep navy-violet gradient with a magenta/blue glow, one violet primary, small warm accents (orange, yellow) for edited letters and cards. Signature moments: the vector shape drawn and turned into a logo, cursors editing letters inside a giant headline, the phone exploding into isometric layers with numbered labels, the tilted canvas of many screens, the CTA button bursting into pixels and blooming to white, and the end card that repeats the opening build.
look: 2.5D, not real 3D: flat UI cards, flat type and flat vector shapes, placed on planes in true perspective for the layer stack and the tilted canvas; translucent frosted-glass layers with thin bright edges; no cast shadows beyond soft drop glows under cards and buttons; soft bloom and glow on buttons and on light transitions; depth of field only as edge blur on the tilted canvas; heavy motion blur on whips and zoom-throughs; backgrounds are either a near-white lavender canvas with faint editor rulers or a deep navy-to-violet radial gradient with a soft magenta/blue glow, no ground plane.
code_translation: Code-native. Built in HTML/CSS/SVG in headless Chromium: SVG path drawing (stroke-dashoffset, anchor handles) for the pen-tool build; masked rising text (overflow-hidden line boxes, translateY from 100%) with the shaped brand Persian font, never splitting joined letters; CSS 3D transforms (perspective, rotateX/rotateZ, translateZ per layer) or three.js planes with UI textures for the isometric layer stack and the tilted canvas; edge blur via a masked backdrop blur; motion blur by frame blending or a directional blur filter during whips; radial zoom blur and bloom via scaled, blurred, screen-blended copies; pixel burst as a small particle layer of squares. Nothing here needs a real 3D render.
continuity: Bookend build: the film opens and closes on the same build-up of a mark (shape drawn → filled → becomes the logo, wordmark rises letter by letter, spec annotations draw in), so the end card answers the opening.
The subject is carried across a hard cut: the chosen object leaves one scene and flies into its slot in the next, so the cut reads as one continuous move.
One object is decomposed into its stacked layers in isometric depth, labelled, then reassembled before the cut.
Choice as motion: several options appear together, one is selected with a box and a cursor click, the others fly out sideways with motion blur.
Action → result through light: a press or typed request blooms into light and the result arrives out of that bloom.
A cursor (or cursors) acts inside the scene — selecting, recolouring letters, pressing — so every change has a visible cause.
Design-spec annotations (bounding boxes, swatches, measurement tags, monospace labels) appear around the key object after it settles, as a texture that says 'built with care'.
Light ↔ dark alternation: scenes swap between a near-white canvas and a deep violet gradient at each hard cut, the cut hidden by a zoom-through, iris, bloom or white flash.
Zoom out from one item to the whole system it belongs to (single screen → tilted canvas of many screens).
Every hard cut and whip is placed on a music accent; the first hard cut is the music drop after a quiet build.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy the 'strata' logo or wordmark, its URL, the English copy, the fintech screens, the balance figure, the brand names on the screens, the cursor names, or the shot order one by one.

Source is 16:9 landscape; a 9:16 film must rebuild each composition vertically (two-line headline above or below the object, layer stack and canvas rotated to fill the height, inside the 9:16 safe zone).

Arrivals are 0.15-0.3 s and holds are 0.5-1 s: Persian text hold times and minimum sizes win over the pace (readability ranks above the reference); the tiny monospace spec labels are texture only and never carry meaning the viewer must read.

Headlines rise from a baseline mask and the reference reads left to right (lines staggered left → right, whips to the left, typing from the left): direction for Persian follows references/rtl-grammar.md, and masked reveals must reveal whole joined words, never letter by letter in a way that breaks Persian joining.
The cursor-recolours-one-letter device does not transfer to joined Persian script letter by letter; apply it to whole words or to a separate Latin/number token.

Reference colours (near-white lavender, deep navy-violet, violet primary, orange/yellow accents, magenta glow) map onto brand colour roles (light background, dark background, primary, accent); never used as literal hex values. Colours were read by eye, not sampled.
The reference has a music track with cuts on its accents; our film's cuts follow the voiceover first, and L6 places accents on our cuts rather than reusing their music.
